newsitem.title: CANADA: Century 21 sees robust housing market in '97, '98.
newsitem.headline: Century 21 sees robust housing market in '97, '98.

text.p: Canadian housing prices and sales volumes will likely stabilize at 1996 levels for at least the next two years, according to a survey by Century 21 Real Estate Canada Ltd.

The survey said the outlook for the residental real estate market in Saskatchewan and Manitoba is the best in the country, and spring of 1997 is likely to be "stronger even than last year's extremely buoyant spring market."
The report credited low interest rates and the likelihood that they will remain low for the positive outlook.
The Bank of Canada in 1996 brought short-term interest rates in Canada to 40-year lows. Five year mortgages at 6.95 percent are now at the lowest since 1965.

"There is a feeling across the country that we are in a long-term economic recovery, with long-term low interest rates, limited or no inflation, and a political climate more stable than it has been for several years," said a statement from Don Lawby, president of Century 21 Real Estate Canada Ltd.

The results of the survey showed that from December 1995 to December 1996 prices increased in 55 areas, decreased in 27, and remained stable in eight. Most price movements were within five precent of the December 1995 survey results.
